The answer's four claims each name branch, metric, period and the right figure or direction, so each is SUPPORTED and the answer is SUPPORTED overall (section 3, IR-1); 'Here is what I found.' is not a claim.

scenarios.title: B15: wrong upstream values are mismatches, including a CAC whose only error is its customer count
scenarios.rationale: Comparable, complete snapshots whose values are wrong must be MISMATCH (section 2, order 5) with the disagreeing dimensions: a CAC whose numerator is right but whose denominator counts a sold-not-serviced or untracked customer (FR-3); a CAC rounded half-even instead of half-up (section 2: the product's value is rounded half-up to the cent, and money must agree to the cent); spend that includes an unmapped campaign (FR-2); invoiced amounts reported under a collected-cash definition (FR-4); an inflated paid-customer count. The correctly rounded CAC and the any-channel new-customer count must still MATCH.

Atlas's denominator of 5 could come from counting d5 (sold, not serviced) or d6 (untracked); either way only the denominator is wrong. Revision is not required on these MISMATCHes; if the runner stamps world records after asOf it may also appear. No paid_cac check is given because the check format states no rounding for $300.125.

scenarios.rationale: Definition differences are not errors (section 2, order 2): a blended CAC (all media spend / any-channel new customers), customers sold instead of serviced, invoice-date cash and a lead-branch CAC each differ from every product definition of their family in named attributes, so INCOMPATIBLE_DEFINITION with those attributes and the product's value for reference, even when the lead-branch value happens to equal the product's. Gross and net payments each have a product definition (section 1 table), so a gross snapshot is compared with Gross payments and a net one with Collected revenue; a net-labelled snapshot carrying the gross figure is a value error (FR-4: a refund reduces collected cash in the month it is paid out).

A reviewer who compares every cash snapshot with Collected revenue only would label it INCOMPATIBLE_DEFINITION (definition.cashBasis); both readings agree it is not a MISMATCH, and MATCH is the reading under which a disagreement scores as a false alarm, not a false certification. (b) For customers sold, the product metric shown for reference (paid customers 4 or new customers serviced 6) is not specified, so no productValue. (c) For invoice-date cash, B09 has no refunds, so the reference figure is $874.00 whether net or gross is shown.

scenarios.title: B22: inputs that cannot be compared are not determinable, a CAD figure is a different definition, and the verdict order decides combinations
scenarios.rationale: Order 1 (NOT_DETERMINABLE) wins over everything below it (section 2): a null currency, office-local days, no definition, an attribute or a family outside the vocabulary, an unknown branch (BRIEF section 4: only B01..B44 exist) or brand, and a reversed period cannot be compared, even when the value happens to equal the product's. A CAD snapshot is INCOMPATIBLE_DEFINITION (order 2): it is neither converted nor compared (FR-6). CAD plus office-local days is still NOT_DETERMINABLE (order 1 first); CAD plus a different numerator is INCOMPATIBLE with both dimensions; a null currency plus a different numerator is NOT_DETERMINABLE. A correct USD control must MATCH.
scenarios.knownAmbiguity: (a) Required dimensions for NOT_DETERMINABLE are only the obvious ones (currency, definition.periodBasis, scope, period); none is required for a missing definition or an out-of-vocabulary attribute or family. (b) Count snapshots across the pack carry currency USD, because the contract treats a null currency as NOT_DETERMINABLE without exempting counts. (c) No productValue on CAD snapshots: the product's USD figure is not in the snapshot's unit. (d) Whether the CAD figure is a conversion of $540.00 is irrelevant: it is never converted.
